cards.text: This is Psalm 145, a psalm of praise from David, Israel's king. The man runs a whole kingdom, and he opens by talking straight to God and calling Him "my God and King."

cards.question: King David has a King of his own. How long does David say he'll bless God's name?

answers.text: For the rest of his reign

cards.question: David plans to save his praise for the big days, like feasts and victories.

cards.text: Every day, not just the big ones. Then David turns from talking to God to talking about Him: "Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised; His greatness is unsearchable."

cards.question: David says the LORD's greatness is unsearchable. What does he mean?

answers.text: No one can ever reach the end of it
God keeps it hidden from His people
Only kings are able to understand it

cards.text: Friend, I lived in a junk drawer for YEARS and never found the bottom of that pile of old takeout menus, and that was a DRAWER. Now David starts looking ahead to who'll tell of God's mighty acts.

cards.question: David looks way past his own lifetime. He pictures each ___ telling the next one about God's mighty acts.

cards.text: Then David says, "…I will meditate on Your wondrous works." He's not skimming these like a group chat with 400 unread messages.

cards.question: While others proclaim God's awesome deeds, David says he'll declare God's greatness himself.

cards.text: Those generations will celebrate the fame of God's abundant goodness and sing joyfully of His righteousness. That's a LOT of people with one favorite subject, friend.
Then David stops telling you who's talking about God. He tells you what God is actually like.

cards.question: David describes the LORD as quick to anger.

cards.text: "The LORD is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in loving devotion." That's close to how the LORD described Himself to Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 34:6).

cards.question: David just said the LORD is gracious and compassionate. How far does he say the LORD's goodness reaches?

answers.text: Only to those who praise Him

cards.text: Generations of people praising God is already a BIG crowd. Now David widens the circle even more.

cards.question: David says only people will give the LORD thanks.

cards.text: All He has made will give Him thanks, and His saints will bless Him. Then David says they'll tell of the glory of His kingdom and speak of His might.

cards.question: In David's psalm, God's kingdom and might get talked about. What does David say it's for?

answers.text: So people would know His mighty acts
So His enemies would be afraid
So God would reward the speakers

cards.text: Now remember, David's a king himself. And here he is, bragging on Somebody else's kingdom.

cards.question: David says the LORD is faithful in all His words, not just some of them.
David moves from God's kingdom to what this King does for people. What does the LORD do for all who fall or are bowed down?

answers.text: He holds them up and lifts them
He waits for them to stand alone
He sends someone else to help

cards.text: Then David pictures the eyes of all looking to the LORD. Like a whole room of coworkers watching the door, waiting on the boss to walk in.

cards.question: All eyes look to the LORD. What does He give them?

cards.text: "You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing." Every. Living. Thing. Not one creature left out.

cards.question: David says the LORD is kind only to the people who earn it.

cards.text: Then David takes on a question a lot of us carry around. How close is God, really?

cards.question: Who does David say the LORD is near to?

answers.text: Those who call on Him in truth
Those who serve in the temple

cards.question: For those who fear the LORD, what does He do when they cry out?

answers.text: He hears them and saves them
He tests them a while longer
He tells them to wait quietly

cards.question: David draws a line between those who love the LORD and the wicked. He says the LORD preserves both groups.

cards.text: And David ends right where he started, with his own mouth declaring the praise of the LORD. 'Forever and ever' shows up again, just like in his first two lines.

cards.question: In his last line, David calls on every ___ to bless the LORD's holy name forever and ever.
